CHIEF COMPLAINT
Routine yearly exam

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
This is Christine, a 63-year-old female presenting for her routine yearly physical examination. Patient reports that her depression is doing well. She is compliant with her prescribed antidepressant medication and attends therapy weekly, which has been helpful for symptom management. She denies suicidal ideation. Sleep is good with eight hours nightly. Regarding her hypertension history, she reports her blood pressure has been fluctuating over the past couple of weeks, with readings that are either elevated or low, and have not remained stable despite medication adherence. She attributes some headaches to prolonged computer screen use. Patient notes her diet has been suboptimal lately due to increased work stress and longer work hours, resulting in frequent consumption of frozen meals rather than prepared home-cooked meals. She has not had time for grocery shopping or meal preparation.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
Patient reports her right carpal tunnel release from approximately two years ago is doing well with no numbness or tingling in her hands or fingers. Denies significant headaches beyond those attributed to screen time. No other systems reviewed.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
1. Hypertension
2. Depression
3. Carpal tunnel syndrome, status post right carpal tunnel release approximately 2 years ago

MEDICATIONS
1. Antidepressant (prescribed by physician)
2. Lisinopril (to be increased)

ALLERGIES
Not documented

FAMILY HISTORY
Not documented

SOCIAL HISTORY
Patient works with computers and reports spending significant time looking at computer screens daily. She has recently increased her work hours and is experiencing work-related stress. Diet consists primarily of frozen meals due to time constraints.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
General: Exam essentially normal
Lungs: Clear bilaterally
Neck: No adenopathy, no evidence of hyperthyroidism
Cardiovascular: Regular rate and rhythm, no murmurs
Neurological: Grips equal and strong bilaterally, neurologically intact, strength good throughout
Pulses: Good bilaterally

RESULTS
Vital Signs: Blood pressure elevated in office today
Labs: All essentially normal

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
1. Hypertension: Patient has persistently elevated blood pressure despite medication compliance. Will increase lisinopril from current dose to 10 mg once daily. Patient instructed to monitor blood pressure at home. Follow-up appointment in one month to reassess blood pressure control.

2. Depression: Currently stable on present medication regimen with good therapy compliance. No medication changes at this time. Continue current antidepressant and weekly therapy.

3. Carpal tunnel syndrome, right wrist: Status post release approximately 2 years ago with excellent recovery and no current symptoms. Patient instructed to report any recurrence of tingling or numbness.
